title: Air-gapped operator handshake and scheduled mirror fallback PRD
creator: Maya R. Patel
description: PRD to define requirements and acceptance criteria for an operator-level handshake protocol and a timebound local mirror fallback strategy for Private/VPC (air-gapped or minimal-egress) deployments. Purpose: enable safe, verifiable upgrades and artifact distribution when egress must be tightly constrained or fully disabled. Focus areas: secure operator bootstrap handshake, signed artifact mirroring, scheduled mirror refresh windows, deterministic rollback triggers, and operator observability hooks.
background: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs or air-gapped environments require upgrade and artifact distribution flows that do not assume persistent egress. Existing approaches (ephemeral proxy, ad-hoc manual mirror) are brittle for larger fleets and create operational cost. This PRD defines a reproducible, operator-driven handshake and scheduled mirror mechanism that minimizes required egress windows, provides cryptographic provenance, and supports automated rollback when integrity or network expectations fail.
goals: Define a two-phase operator handshake that negotiates allowed egress windows and mirror URIs with customer operator agents
Specify a timebound mirror refresh protocol (local registry or OCI mirror) that supports staged pull, checksum verification, and signature validation
Produce concrete acceptance criteria for zero/low-egress upgrades, including observability and rollback triggers
Minimize manual steps for customers: provide CLI/operator automation to configure mirror schedule and validate state before upgrades
non_goals: Building new long-term CDN or global image distribution infrastructure
Replacing customer-managed on-prem artifact distribution workflows entirely
Completing cloud-provider specific network appliance integrations (these will be documented as optional adapters)
requirements: Operator handshake must complete without outbound egress except to a short list of allowlisted management endpoints; the handshake should negotiate a single scheduled window (start/end UTC) and return a signed token valid only for that window
Mirror artifacts (images, charts, operator manifests) must be signed with Redwood image signing and include provenance metadata (source commit, build id, signature URL)
Mirror refresh protocol shall support incremental staged sync: metadata first, then artifacts in prioritized order (control plane components, CRDs, operators, runtime images)
Upgrade orchestration shall validate checksums and signatures before applying any changes; a failed validation must abort and leave cluster in pre-upgrade state
Operator must support a 'dry-run' handshake mode that validates allowed routing without performing pulls
Fallback behavior: if the scheduled mirror window is missed or partial, operator can revert to previous known-good revision automatically or queue for manual approval depending on customer policy
All handshake and mirror actions must be logged to local audit logs and optionally emitted to configured telemetry endpoints when allowed
Configuration surface: CLI flags and operator CRD fields to declare mirror URIs, allowed egress CIDRs, scheduled window, signature verification policy, and automated rollback policy
acceptance_criteria: Given an isolated VPC with only an allowlist for a single mirror host, operator completes handshake and downloads manifest metadata within the scheduled 30-minute window
During a staged upgrade test, operator validates signatures for all artifacts; if any signature mismatch occurs, upgrade halts and cluster remains at prior revision
In an emulated network partition where only partial artifacts are available, operator rolls back to last stable release within the configured rollback timeout without manual intervention
Dry-run handshake validates routing and token issuance without initiating any pulls and reports 'VALID' to operator status conditions
Audit logs contain timestamped entries for handshake start/finish, token issuance, per-artifact checksum validation, and final upgrade result
Upgrade scenario with expired scheduled window fails fast and surfaces clear remediation steps in operator status and logs
Customer-facing CLI documentation and operator CRD schema reviewed and approved by Security and TechDocs owners
rollback_criteria: Artifact signature or checksum verification failure
Mirror refresh incomplete after two attempts across distinct allowlisted mirrors
Post-upgrade health checks for control-plane or runtime components fail to converge within configured grace period
Operator crashloop or repeated reconciliation errors during upgrade phase
telemetry_and_alerting: Alert: handshake_token_expiration_mismatch (firing when token valid period differs from scheduled window)
Alert: mirror_sync_failure_rate > 5% over 1 hour in a customer deployment
Log fields: handshake_id, mirror_uri, artifact_path, signature_url, checksum, verification_result
notes_and_tradeoffs: We prioritize cryptographic validation and deterministic rollback over minimizing window duration; tradeoff is slightly longer engineer-run windows during initial rollout. We will iterate on allowlist compression and token pinning to reduce blast radius. For large fleets, recommend mirror hierarchy (regional mirrors) but those integrations are out of scope for the first cut.
how_to_validate_in_staging: Provision a test VPC with strict egress allowlist pointing to a staging mirror
Run CLI handshake in dry-run mode and assert operator status condition 'handshake:valid'
Trigger scheduled mirror window and run a full staged upgrade to a canary operator revision
Simulate signature corruption and assert rollback behavior and alert firing
